Gauntlet loop · whole house

The real house, rebuilt room by room until a critic stops telling them apart

Every room of this house is being rebuilt as procedural 3D geometry inside the live Home Assistant app, then screenshotted from the same spot the reference photo was taken. A separate critic with fresh context puts the two side by side, blind, and says which is which. If ours is obvious, it goes back to the builder. The bar for the overall look is The Sims 4's dollhouse build view; the bar for each room is the photograph of that actual room.

0 of 18 rooms past the critic  ·  paused at an API session limit · partial work verified intact

Rooms

Master Bedroom

With critic

The bed is a KING. Round 3 had 'proved' a queen from photo anchors and that was carried for three rounds; the measurement had been taken against a headboard 25 degrees off square, foreshortened by a quarter. Re-measured against objects at the same depth, the shams are 36-inch king pillows. The invented white chest was deleted for the armchair the photo and plan both show, a TV added, soft surfaces given real texture, and the room slimmed from 3.41 MB to 1.74 MB. It also found a bug in the shared GLB library and independently confirmed the entry vestibule was misplaced.

Kitchen

Rejected

Critic FAILED round 3. The counter stone still reads as marks rather than a field — high-pass energy 0.25 against the photograph's 0.40 to 0.48 — and the room had grown to 5.88 MB, 27 percent of the whole house, spent on the very tone fields that made it worse. It did adjudicate both of the builder's disagreements in the builder's favour. Round 4 was interrupted mid-build.

Living Room

Rejected

Critic FAILED round 4 and found the flaw at the centre of the whole loop: standard deviation is scale-blind. Every fabric and masonry surface here matches the photograph's sd and is 3 to 7 times too smooth at the scale a person actually sees — upholstery 1.62 against 11.84 measured as mean difference between adjacent pixels. It also found two of round 4's fixes were regressions caused by chasing a metric: the east canvas was re-toned until its value ratio was right and ended up a blank slab, and stone relief was deleted because restoring it raised sd. Round 5 was interrupted mid-build.

Dining

With critic

Rebuilt into the re-traced polygon. Verified orientation three independent ways and confirmed round 1 had it right. The bay is real now, so its three windows sit on the actual canted facets as cut holes, and both doorways are true passages — and it registered the kitchen doorway to the exact world span room 6 had already cut on its own side, so the two rooms' holes align instead of each showing the other's jamb. The 7.8 ft table fits without being shrunk: at that size the west end chair sits in the bay mouth exactly where the photo puts it.

Rios Room

With critic

Round 2 found the room was 180 degrees out, not merely too big: re-deriving orientation from the floor plan against two adjacencies puts the windows on the SOUTH wall. It also found there are two rubber trees, one at each end of the window wall, which is why round 1's corner never resolved. Windows rebuilt to 4.85 ft tall with a 1 ft header as measured, cut as real openings; the room-filling emissive wall wash deleted rather than re-tuned, and the room now meters within a few points of an empty room of the same size — it is no longer compensating for the renderer.

Office

With critic

The first room built with per-wall albedo skins, and they closed the problem every previous critic named: the four walls went from N 234 / W 210 / E 171 / S 149, a spread of 85.5, down to a spread of 22.9 — real rooms sit within about 30. Its orientation check against the floor plan also caught two errors the shell pass had made: only one window where there are two, and an invented door on the west wall that is actually the bathroom party wall.

Guest Room

With critic

The sixth room whose orientation turned out wrong: the shell pass had it 180 degrees out on Z, with the headboard, closet and dresser all on the wrong walls. Proved three ways — registering the plan to world coordinates and sampling the bed and pillow icons, a camera solve from seven identifiable points at rms 1.16 degrees (the rival positions score 18.3), and the round mirror, which reflects the blinded window and a picture and therefore faces west. Payload 0.563 MB, the lightest furnished room in the house.

Laundry

With critic

Structural correction: the shell pass had put the washer and dryer at the west end of the north wall, which is exactly where the plan puts the step and door in from the garage. Moved east to the plan's own appliance icon. Honest caveat recorded: the traced footprint merges the real mudroom and laundry alcove, so no camera inside it can reproduce the photo — the side-by-side is a content match, not a geometry match. Spread 89.6 to 18.2.

Pantry

With critic

Both photographs show the doors closed, so the entire interior is inferred: five-tier shelving on the wall you face through the doors, stocked, with a step stool. Only one wall yields a clean metering field, so the skins were sized from the laundry's set scaled by the two rooms' bare west walls, which agree to 3 percent.

Movie Room

With critic

Geometry derived by thresholding the basement floor plan into an ASCII map at 14px cells, giving a uniform 35.85 px/ft scale, then cross-checked against the live stairs row — which independently confirmed the east wall is solid exactly where the stair runs and open where the newel post appears in the photo. Sectional, screen wall with console and subwoofers, art run, real cut window and stairwell passage. All four walls metered: average 189.0 against the photo's 190.3.

Arcade Room

With critic

The plan's only wall gap between the two basement rooms pins the photographer's position, and a 5.3 x 6.5 ft utility room in the footprint's north-west corner explains the photo's far wall. Eleven arcade cabinets from one model varied by marquee and side-art to stay inside the payload budget. It also caught a structural error: the shell pass had drawn the door leaf 2.4 ft away from where the actual opening was cut.

Garage

With critic

No interior photograph of this garage exists, and the report says so plainly. What is measured: the sectional door and layout from the plan and the exterior shots. What is inferred: the workbench run, water heater, freezer, mower, bike, bins and the car — a light silver saloon deliberately, since the household SUV is the one parked on the driveway outside. Wall spread 91.5 to 12.3, the best in the house.
